headers.description: Optional headers to send with the request as a dictionary of header values.

Content-Type.description: The media type of the resource being requested, typically 'application/json'.

Authorization.description: The credentials to authenticate a user agent with a server, typically formatted as 'Bearer {token}'.

timeout.description: The maximum amount of time to wait for a response from the server, in seconds. A longer timeout may be necessary for slower network connections or overloaded servers. This is a float type value.

params.description: URL parameters to append to the URL. Sent as a dictionary of key-value pairs.

query.description: The query parameter for search or filtering.

page.description: The page number parameter for pagination. Used to retrieve a specific page of results.

auth.description: HTTP authentication credentials formatted as a (username, password) tuple.

cert.description: Path to the SSL client certificate file (.pem), if required for the request.

cookies.description: Cookies to send with the request as a dictionary of cookie names and values.

sessionid.description: Session identifier cookie, used to recognize client sessions on the server.

csrftoken.description: CSRF protection token cookie, used to prevent cross-site request forgery attacks.

proxies.description: Proxy settings as a dictionary, mapping protocol or protocol and hostname to the URL of the proxy.

http.description: Proxy URL to use for HTTP requests, including the port number.

https.description: Proxy URL to use for HTTPS requests, including the port number.

stream.description: Whether to stream the download of the response. If False, the response content will be immediately downloaded. Streaming is useful for handling large files or responses.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate or not. Set to False to skip certificate verification, which is not recommended unless you are sure of the server's identity.

Below are a handful of public IP‑lookup APIs that expose **organization/company** data (and often include contact details such as domain, email, phone, etc.). All of them offer a free tier (or a trial) so you can try them out before committing to a paid plan. | Service | Key Features | Typical Free Tier | How to Get Started | |---------|--------------|-------------------|--------------------| | **ipinfo.io** | • Organization name
• Domain
• Email & phone (if available)
• ASN, carrier, timezone, etc. | 50 000 requests/month (no key needed for basic lookup) | Sign up → Get API key → Use `https://ipinfo.io//json?token=` | | **ipstack.com** | • Company name & domain
• Contact email & phone (paid plans only)
• Location, currency, timezone, etc. | 10 000 requests/month (free plan) | Sign up → Get API key → Use `http://api.ipstack.com/?access_key=&format=1` | | **ipapi.co** | • Organization & domain
• Email & phone (paid plans)
• Geo‑data, currency, etc. | 30 000 requests/month (free plan) | Sign up → Get API key → Use `https://ipapi.co//json/?key=` | | **ipgeolocation.io** | • Company name, domain, email, phone
• ASN, carrier, timezone, etc. | 1 000 requests/day (free plan) | Sign up → Get API key → Use `https://api.ipgeolocation.io/ipgeo?apiKey=&ip=` | | **ipdata.co** | • Organization, domain, email, phone
• ASN, carrier, threat intel, etc. | 1 500 requests/day (free plan) | Sign up → Get API key → Use `https://api.ipdata.co/?api-key=` | | **ipwhois.io** | • Organization, domain, email, phone (paid plans)
• ASN, carrier, location, etc. | 10 000 requests/month (free plan) | Sign up → Get API key → Use `https://ipwhois.app/json/?key=` | --- ### Quick Example (Python) ```python import requests def lookup_ip(ip, api_key=None): # Example using ipinfo.io url = f"https://ipinfo.io/{ip}/json" params = {"token": api_key} if api_key else {} r = requests.get(url, params=params, timeout=5) r.raise_for_status() return r.json() # Replace with your own key if you have one data = lookup_ip("8.8.8.8", api_key="YOUR_IPINFO_TOKEN") print(data) ``` Typical JSON response (fields vary by provider): ```json { "ip": "8.8.8.8", "hostname": "dns.google", "city": "Mountain View", "region": "California", "country": "US", "loc": "37.3860,-122.0840", "org": "AS15169 Google LLC", "postal": "94035", "timezone": "America/Los_Angeles", "readme": "https://ipinfo.io/missingauth" } ``` If you’re looking for **contact email or phone**, you’ll usually need to upgrade to a paid plan (e.g., ipinfo.io’s “Pro” plan, ipstack’s “Business” plan, etc.). The free tiers generally return the organization name and domain, but not the detailed contact info. --- ### Choosing the Right One | Criteria | ipinfo.io | ipstack.com | ipapi.co | ipgeolocation.io | ipdata.co | |----------|-----------|-------------|----------|------------------|-----------| | **Free tier** | 50k req/mo | 10k req/mo | 30k req/mo | 1k req/day | 1.5k req/day | | **Contact email/phone** | Paid only | Paid only | Paid only | Paid only | Paid only | | **Ease of use** | Very simple | Simple | Simple | Simple | Simple | | **Pricing (paid)** | $9/mo (1M req) | $99/mo (1M req) | $49/mo (1M req) | $19/mo (1M req) | $29/mo (1M req) | | **Best for quick trials** | ✔️ | ✔️ | ✔️ | ✔️ | ✔️ | --- #### Next Steps 1. Pick a provider that fits your budget and feature needs. 2. Sign up for an account and grab your API key. 3. Use the endpoint shown above (replace `` and ``). 4. Parse the JSON response to extract `org`, `domain`, `email`, `phone`, etc. Happy coding!
